headword: {丁重|ていちょう}に{断|ことわ}る
reading: ていちょうにことわる
gloss: to politely decline; to turn down gracefully

definitions.gloss: to politely decline; to turn down gracefully
definitions.explanation: To refuse an offer, invitation, or request in a respectful and considerate manner, showing regard for the other person's feelings.

examples.japanese: お{誘|さそ}いを{丁重|ていちょう}に{断|ことわ}った。
{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}なさそうに、{丁重|ていちょう}に{断|ことわ}られた。
examples.english: I was turned down gracefully, with an apologetic manner.

examples.japanese: {取引先|とりひきさき}からの{提案|ていあん}を、{理由|りゆう}を{述|の}べて{丁重|ていちょう}に{断|ことわ}ることが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It is important to politely decline a proposal from a business partner by stating your reasons.

notes:
A set phrase combining {丁重|ていちょう} (polite, courteous) with {断|ことわ}る (to refuse). This is the standard way to describe refusing something while maintaining politeness and respect. Essential in Japanese business and social contexts where outright refusal is considered rude.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{申|もう}し{出|で}を{丁重|ていちょう}に{断|ことわ}る — to politely decline an offer
- {丁重|ていちょう}にお{断|ことわ}りする — to politely refuse (humble form)
- {依頼|いらい}を{丁重|ていちょう}に{断|ことわ}る — to politely decline a request

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- やんわり{断|ことわ}る — to refuse softly/gently; less formal than {丁重|ていちょう}に
- きっぱり{断|ことわ}る — to refuse firmly/decisively; the opposite approach
- {遠慮|えんりょ}する — to decline; more indirect and softer

REGISTER:
Appropriate for formal and business situations. In casual contexts, やんわり{断|ことわ}る is more natural.
